chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariya al-Qattan told us, saying: Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib told us, saying: Tamim ibn Buhloul told us, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, saying: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):

Indeed, upon me is much debt, and I have dependents and I am not able to perform the pilgrimage, so teach me a supplication that I may pray with. So he said: Say at the end of every prescribed prayer: 'O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad, and clear me of the debt of this world and the debt of the Hereafter.' Then I said to him: As for the debt of this world, I have known it, so what is the debt of the Hereafter? He said: The debt of the Hereafter is the pilgrimage.
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for clearing debt and fulfilling the obligation of Hajj when unable to travel?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides a practical spiritual remedy for those burdened by debt who are unable to perform Hajj, linking the physical obligation of pilgrimage to a broader theological concept of 'debt.' By prescribing a specific supplication after every obligatory prayer, the Imam emphasizes that Hajj is not merely a ritual but a fundamental debt owed to God in the Hereafter, the clearance of which is essential for spiritual completeness. This teaching underscores the Shia scholarly view that spiritual obligations often parallel and sometimes substitute for material ones in times of hardship.
